name: Untouchables
label: Dischord
lede: Ian MacKaye's kid brother sang, a drummer who'd never played drums took over mid-band, and the singer kept passing out. Sonic Youth covered their best song eleven years after they quit.

eras.title: The Teen Idles' little brothers
eras.text: Wilson High School in Northwest D.C. produced most of the city's first hardcore bands. The Untouchables were the younger crew, close friends with the Teen Idles, fronted by Alec MacKaye, Teen Idle Ian MacKaye's little brother.

years.h: Ian MacKaye's kid brother gets a band of his own
years.p: [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]], born in 1965, sings. [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] plays guitar, [[Bert Queiroz|d657171b-961c-4078-ab84-90b2c69f0095]] bass and Rich Moore drums.

years.h: Debut in a basement, on a bill with [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]]
years.p: Dischord says the two bands debuted together in a basement in December 1979. The crowd was the same handful of friends on both sides of the stage.
years.xp: Both bands came out of Wilson High School in Northwest D.C., and Alec was the younger brother of Teen Idles singer [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]. Dischord gives the month and the basement, not the address.

eras.title: Passing out, holding on
eras.text: The Untouchables played hard and mostly at home. 1980 brought their only recordings, one road trip to Norfolk, and a crisis when drummer Rich Moore left for college that nearly ended them.

yt: Full set at d.c. space, Dec. 17, 1980
years.h: Alec MacKaye hyperventilates, passes out, gets carried out
years.p: It happened at a number of Untouchables shows, according to Dischord. The set didn't need a stunt.
years.xp: Dischord's history of the band says Alec "had to be carried out of a number of shows after hyperventilating and passing out." The footage of a full set at d.c. space in December 1980 is the closest look at what those shows were like.

years.big: "The band decided it was curtains for them."
years.h: The band meets at Roy Rogers to quit; Danny Ingram volunteers
years.p: When Rich Moore leaves for college, the Untouchables lose their drummer and their practice space. [[Danny Ingram|41959411-d1b4-4954-af09-087ac72f69ab]] offers to play, though he has never played drums.
years.xp:
Dischord calls the Roy Rogers "a central punk hangout at the time." The line above is Dischord's own summary of the meeting, not a band member's quote.

Ingram's offer kept the Untouchables going into 1981. His drumming career went on through [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]], [[Strange Boutique|0ee0668b-fa1d-4db1-ac8c-43a3ad1272c0]], [[Dot Dash|fce03e2d-8138-4418-b29e-499f61c6800e]] and, per Wikipedia, [[Swervedriver|fa6c7999-ff65-486b-9e18-bcb59d6db2f0]].

years.h: One road trip, to Norfolk, Virginia, with the Teen Idles
years.p: Everything else the Untouchables played was in D.C. Dischord doesn't date the Norfolk show.

eras.title: Until the plug was pulled
eras.text: The Untouchables ended the way they played: on someone else's gear at someone else's show at the 9:30 club. Within months the members were all over the next wave of D.C. bands, from Youth Brigade to Faith.

years.h: The Untouchables borrow the stage at the 9:30 club and get unplugged
years.p: During a [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]] and [[Black Market Baby|5fcf3f0f-0945-4269-a6a5-9f63c385c1f4]] show, they grab the gear and play a [[Sham 69|33235ed4-d5bd-42cd-b77c-de646c36c8c6]] song until the plug is pulled. That's the last Untouchables show.
years.xp: Dischord dates it only as early 1981. Wikipedia puts the band's end in January 1981.

years.h: The boy on the front of Minor Threat's first EP is Alec
years.p: Alec MacKaye, the Untouchables' singer, is on the cover of [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]'s first record. The image returns on the Complete Discography.

years.cap: Alec MacKaye singing with the Faith at the Chancery, Washington, D.C., 1982
years.h: Youth Brigade takes the rhythm section; Faith takes the singer
years.p: Danny Ingram and Bert Queiroz join [[Nathan Strejcek|b53e7b75-696d-43f5-98ff-bc3d104e0d74]] in [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]]. By fall 1981, Alec MacKaye is singing for [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] with SOA veterans Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson.

years.h: Three Untouchables songs open Flex Your Head after the Teen Idles
years.p: Rat Patrol, Nic Fit and I Hate You come from spring 1980 demos made in the Hit & Run basement studio.
years.xp: The Untouchables and the Teen Idles recorded their first demos at Hit & Run in spring 1980, and the tapes got passed around the D.C. scene before Dischord put three songs on Flex Your Head.

eras.title: Nic Fit, eleven years on
eras.text: A band with four recorded songs kept turning up in places nobody expected, most loudly when Sonic Youth covered the Untouchables' Nic Fit on the major-label album Dirty.

years.h: Sonic Youth put a 1980 basement song on a DGC album
years.p: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] cover the Untouchables' Nic Fit on Dirty, their 1992 album.
years.xp:
By then the Untouchables were long into other lives. Eddie Janney had played in [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]], [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] and more; Bert Queiroz and Rich Moore had both played in [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] and started R&B Records together.

Alec MacKaye went on to [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]] and [[The Warmers|af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f]], and works as chief preparator at the Phillips Collection in Washington.

years.h: 20 Years of Dischord collects them again
years.p: Dischord includes the Untouchables on its anniversary box set and the rare-and-unreleased collection that goes with it.
The song is featured in the documentary built on Steven Blush's oral history.
